Record Class PanelPosition

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.PanelPosition
public record PanelPosition(PanelPosition.Mode mode, @Nullable String anchorPanelId, @Nullable ScreenRegion screenAnchor, @Nullable MenuRegion menuRegion, @Nullable Supplier<ScreenOrigin> pixelOrigin) extends Record
Describes how a panel is positioned within a screen's layout.

Movement ③ — the main-panel + region model. A custom screen names ONE panel as its main = its frame (centred on the screen, exactly like a vanilla container's menu frame). Every other panel anchors to that frame with a region — the SAME MenuRegion vocabulary and the SAME RegionMath resolver vanilla-injected panels use against the menu frame — so siblings inherit overlay-centring (①) and vertical edge-awareness + auto-scroll (②) for free. This retired the old relative verbs (rightOf / leftOf / above / below), which were a second, edge-unaware placement system bolted onto this enum.

Modes:

  • PanelPosition.Mode.BODY — stacks vertically in a single centred column (default; the legacy regime for simple standalone screens with no designated main panel).
  • PanelPosition.Mode.MAIN — the screen's frame: one per screen, centred, the anchor every REGION sibling resolves against.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.REGION — anchored to the main panel via a MenuRegion (RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP, BOTTOM_CENTER, …), resolved by RegionMath against the main panel's bounds.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.SCREEN_ANCHOR — pinned to a fixed screen corner (chrome).
  • PanelPosition.Mode.CENTER — a screen-centred overlay, drawn on top.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.PIXEL — pixel-precision override: the outer origin comes from a per-frame consumer supplier, in absolute screen pixels. The precision escape for positions regions can't express (§0057 Revision); see pixel(Supplier).

This is declarative metadata. The screen reads it during layout computation to determine where each panel goes.

  • Method Details

    • main

      public static PanelPosition main()
      The screen's main panel = its frame (Movement ③). Centred on the screen window; every region(MenuRegion) sibling anchors to its bounds. Exactly one panel per screen should be main().

    • region

      public static PanelPosition region(MenuRegion region)
      Anchors the panel to the main panel via region (Movement ③) — the same MenuRegion vocabulary vanilla-injected panels use against the menu frame. RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP sits it to the right of the main panel, top- aligned; BOTTOM_CENTER below it, centred; and so on. Resolved by RegionMath against the main panel's bounds, so it is edge-aware on both axes and auto-scrolls when it would overflow the screen.

    • screenAnchor

      public static PanelPosition screenAnchor(ScreenRegion region)
      Pins the panel to a fixed screen-edge spot (Pass 3) — inset by RegionConstants.SCREEN_EDGE_MARGIN from the edges that spot touches. The canonical screen-chrome placement: a "< Back" button at TOP_LEFT, a title at TOP_CENTER, a status line at BOTTOM_CENTER. Positioned independently of the layout (contributes nothing to its extent), so it stays put no matter how content sizes, wraps, or scrolls.

      Honored by both MKScreen (the standalone screen) and MainRegionLayout (a custom container screen), via RegionMath.resolveScreenRegion(ScreenRegion, int, int, int, int, int) — the SAME screen-edge placement in either context.

    • center

      public static PanelPosition center()
      Centres the panel on the screen as an overlay — excluded from the layout, auto-centred on the screen window, and drawn on top. The canonical placement for dialogs, popovers, and any panel that floats over the screen instead of flowing in its column.

      Position only: it composes freely with the dimsBehind (visual dim), opaque (click-eat), and tracksAsModal (input-block) flags per the M9 doctrine — a panel can be a centred overlay with any, all, or none of them. Honored by MKScreen.

    • pixel

      public static PanelPosition pixel(Supplier<ScreenOrigin> origin)
      Pixel-precision position override (§0057 Revision — Trev's call, 2026-07-01): places the panel's outer top-left (the background origin; elements render inside at origin + padding) at exactly the coordinates origin supplies, in absolute screen pixels.

      Re-evaluated every frame. The supplier runs on each layout/render pass, so an origin computed from live state — a resolved vanilla slot rect (VanillaSlotResolver.resolve(AbstractContainerScreen, int)), a hovered hotbar column, a user-mutable count — tracks that state with no consumer re-registration. Returning null skips the panel this frame (not rendered, not hit-testable) — the natural "this screen doesn't surface my anchor" escape, e.g. when a slot resolver comes back empty.

      The precision escape, not the default. Declarative regions remain the placement model (§0057); pixel(...) exists for the positions regions cannot express — a point inside the content frame, or an origin that is genuinely dynamic per frame. Unlike the deleted lambda-anchor escape hatch (a parallel placement system at the adapter layer), this is a position KIND inside the one model: resolved by the same drivers, riding the same render/input/opacity machinery as every other panel.

      No reactive budgets. A pixel panel measures at its natural size — the engine feeds it no screen-edge wrap/scroll ceiling, because pixel placement means the consumer owns the exact geometry (§0057's reactive default would fight the precision). Keeping it on-screen is the supplier's contract.

      Honored by the vanilla-screen injection path (ScreenPanelAdapter — including MKCContainerPanel parity panels), MainRegionLayout (custom screens with a main() frame), and MKScreen's legacy path. (The legacy BODY-stack path on a custom container screen predates every non-BODY mode and does not resolve them — use main() there.)

      Parameters:
      origin - per-frame supplier of the panel's outer top-left in absolute screen pixels; null return = skip this frame
